references.text: Solomon's wisdom on getting one's work ready and planning before building: "Finish your outdoor work first, get everything ready in the field, and then build your house" ([ref:Prov 24:27|Proverbs 24:27]). This is a direct parallel to Jesus' parable about counting the cost before building a tower.

The proverb emphasizes the value of careful planning: "The plans of the diligent lead only to abundance, but everyone who rushes ends in poverty" ([ref:Prov 21:5|Proverbs 21:5]). Jesus applies this same principle of careful consideration in his parable about counting the cost of following him.
Joshua sent spies to Jericho to assess the situation before the conquest—an example of wise planning and preparation before a major undertaking ([ref:Josh 2:1|Joshua 2:1–24]).

The following parable of the king who considers whether he can meet an enemy coming with twenty thousand troops with only ten thousand provides a parallel illustration of this same principle of weighing the cost before making a commitment ([ref:Luke 14:31-32|Luke 14:31–32]).

Jesus draws the conclusion from these two parables: "In the same way, none of you can be my disciple unless he gives up everything he owns" ([ref:Luke 14:33|Luke 14:33]). This shows that the parable of the tower builder is about calculating the full cost of following Jesus as a disciple.

Three people who want to follow Jesus but have not considered what it will cost. Jesus warns them that following him requires total commitment ([ref:Luke 9:57-62|Luke 9:57–62]). This illustrates exactly what the parable in verse 28 is about: counting the cost of discipleship.

"Plans are established by taking counsel" ([ref:Prov 20:18|Proverbs 20:18]). This wisdom saying about seeking advice and planning carefully corresponds with Jesus' point about carefully calculating the costs before starting a building project.

The verse just before the parable sets out the radical demands of discipleship: to carry one's cross and give up one's closest family members. The parable of the tower builder in verse 28 serves as an illustration of why these demands must be carefully considered ([ref:Luke 14:26-27|Luke 14:26–27]).
